answer: We formulate dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices where each identity inlet must lock staking collateral backed by zero-knowledge verifiable delay primitives. Capital barrier analysis proves Sybil identity multiplication across the adversarial garden yields strictly negative expected utility, as actors cannot breach cipher defenses to evade massive slashing penalties. Consequently, multi-agent environments converge to a robust Nash equilibrium, as these negative expected payoffs preclude any profitable deviation.
